title: Sheafification preserves flatness of module presheaves
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site, let $\mathcal O$ be a presheaf of commutative rings, and let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules. Assume that tensoring with $\mathcal F$ over $\mathcal O$ preserves finite limits in the category of presheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules. Let $\mathcal O^\#$ and $\mathcal F^\#$ be the associated sheaves, with the induced $\mathcal O^\#$-module structure. Then tensoring with $\mathcal F^\#$ over $\mathcal O^\#$ preserves finite limits in the category of sheaves of $\mathcal O^\#$-modules [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]; equivalently, $\mathcal F^\#$ is flat.

proof.text: Let $\iota$ be restriction of scalars from sheaves of $\mathcal O^\#$-modules to presheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules, and let $a=(-)^\#$ be the module sheafification $\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal O)\to\Mod(\mathcal O^\#)$, left adjoint to $\iota$, whose underlying abelian sheaf is the abelian sheafification [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface]. Finite limits in $\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal O)$ are computed sectionwise, and in $\Mod(\mathcal O^\#)$ they are computed sectionwise and the forgetful functor to abelian sheaves commutes with them [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]; so both forgetful functors to (pre)sheaves of abelian groups preserve and reflect finite limits (a cone of modules is a limit cone iff its underlying cone of abelian (pre)sheaves is). On underlying abelian (pre)sheaves, $\iota$ is the inclusion of sheaves into presheaves and $a$ is abelian sheafification, both of which preserve finite limits [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact]. Therefore $a$ and $\iota$ preserve finite limits. Since $T_{\mathcal F}=-\otimes_{p,\mathcal O}\mathcal F$ preserves finite limits in $\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal O)$ by hypothesis, the composite $a\circ T_{\mathcal F}\circ\iota$ preserves finite limits.

source.place: Lemma 18.28.3 (Tag 03ET), using the exactness of sheafification

proof.text: For every sheaf $\mathcal G$ of $\mathcal O^\#$-modules, the site-level tensor/sheafification comparison gives a natural isomorphism $\mathcal G\otimes_{\mathcal O^\#}\mathcal F^\#\cong(\iota\mathcal G\otimes_{p,\mathcal O}\mathcal F)^\#$ [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-tensor]. By the definition of the sheaf tensor product, this is exactly $\mathcal G\mapsto a(T_{\mathcal F}(\iota\mathcal G))$.

source.place: Lemma 18.28.3 (Tag 03ET), hint and the definition in Section 03EK

proof.text: By Steps 1 and 2, $\mathcal G\mapsto\mathcal G\otimes_{\mathcal O^\#}\mathcal F^\#$ preserves finite limits on $\Mod(\mathcal O^\#)$. It is additive and, being left adjoint to $\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O^\#}(\mathcal F^\#,-)$, preserves cokernels [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], so it is right exact; an additive functor between abelian categories preserving kernels and cokernels is exact. Hence $\mathcal F^\#$ is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] (and, conversely, exactness of this right exact functor gives preservation of finite limits, which is the stated equivalence).
